item.title: Space Force gives SpaceX latitude on design of $2.3 billion satellite network
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — The U.S. Space Force is giving SpaceX latitude to design one of the military’s new low-Earth orbit satellite networks, setting performance requirements rather than prescribing the number and configuration of spacecraft needed to meet them.

item.title: India’s satcom market is ready for scale as regulation, pricing and use cases align
item.description: India is entering a decisive decade for satellite communications. The market has long been shaped by enterprises, government and broadcast demand, but constrained by limited capacity, high service costs and narrow deployment models. That equation is changing as high-throughput geostationary orbit (GEO) satellites expand, non-GEO constellations prepare for commercial entry and connectivity resilience becomes a strategic requirement across public and private networks.

item.title: Space Cargo Unlimited to fly microgravity payloads on Starfall
item.description: PARIS — Space Cargo Unlimited has signed a contract to fly payloads on SpaceX’s Starfall reentry vehicle as it builds out a broad spectrum of options for microgravity research and manufacturing.

item.title: Space threats prompt Europe to bolster domestic capabilities and strengthen alliances
item.description: PARIS – Growing threats to space systems are prompting European nations to strengthen domestic space capabilities while improving coordination with allies, government officials said at the Novaspace Space Security and Defense Summit.

item.title: Isar Aerospace ready to begin commercial Spectrum launches
item.description: PARIS — German launch startup Isar Aerospace will begin commercial launches of its Spectrum rocket after a successful test flight earlier this month as it works to scale up to meet intense demand.

item.title: Planet wins German federal contract for dedicated constellation services
item.description: PARIS – The German Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) will acquire dedicated Earth-observation capacity from Planet Labs Germany, under a contract announced Sept. 16.

item.title: Hydrosat to provide thermal intelligence through commercial data and sovereign satellites
item.description: PARIS – Hydrosat’s next-generation Osiris constellation will provide thermal infrared observations for government and commercial customers, the company announced Sept. 15 at World Space Business Week.

item.title: Djibouti signs the Artemis Accords as the State Department unveils new space partnership program
item.description: PARIS — Djibouti became the latest country to sign the Artemis Accords as the U.S. State Department rolls out a new program to provide benefits to signatories.

item.title: Isaacman says U.S. return to the moon carries national security stakes
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman made a national security case for America’s return to the moon, telling a military audience that the outcome of the intensifying lunar competition with China could shape alliances, technology standards and perceptions of U.S. power.

item.title: Hernandez-Baquero lays out plan to make Space Force acquisition overhaul work
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — The Space Force’s new acquisition chief says his immediate task is turning the service’s recently completed acquisition overhaul into faster delivery of satellites, weapons and other capabilities.

item.title: Viasat nears prime contract for shared D2D constellation
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — Viasat expects to announce a contract within weeks to build the first satellites for Equatys, the joint venture announced last year with Space42 to pool Mobile Satellite Services spectrum for global direct-to-device services.

item.title: Air Force and Space Force push for scale as supply-chain constraints persist
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — “Scaling” has become a watchword for Air Force and Space Force leaders as they push to field more weapons and space capabilities faster and in greater numbers.

item.title: Space Force chief says Iran war shows service’s expanding combat role
item.description: NATIONAL HARBOR, Md. — The U.S. Space Force played a direct combat role in the war with Iran, with guardians conducting electromagnetic warfare against an adversary in addition to providing satellite communications, navigation and missile warning to U.S. forces, the service’s top general said Sept 15.

item.title: Vega launches two Earth science satellites
item.description: PARIS — A Vega C rocket successfully launched a pair of Earth observation satellites for the European Space Agency and the European Commission on Sept. 14.

item.title: Critical design review cleared for 2027 in-orbit cubesat inspection demo
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — British startup Shield Space has completed the critical design review for Broadsword, a 2027 mission aiming to demonstrate satellite-inspection capabilities that defense customers could have in orbit within nine months of contract signing.

item.title: Companies defend Bromo joint venture
item.description: PARIS — Executives with the three European companies seeking to combine their space businesses say the merger is still needed even as European government funding increases.

item.title: SES and Elveo Mobile plan European D2D satellite factory
item.description: TAMPA, Fla. — SES outlined plans Sept. 15 to establish direct-to-device satellite production capabilities in Europe with Elveo Mobile, aiming to build out a regional supply chain to expand the D2D operator’s low Earth orbit (LEO) constellation.

item.title: HawkEye 360 addresses sovereign demand with European entity and partners
item.description: PARIS – HawkEye 360 is addressing growing demand for sovereign space capabilities by establishing a European subsidiary, working with Leonardo to provide radio-frequency sensing to European customers and collaborating with ERA, part of the Czech Republic’s Omnipol Group, the company announced Sept. 15.
